name: PipelineDB
long_description: PipelineDB is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that enables realtime reporting use cases by continuously aggregating large streams of time series data down into summary data. It shines the most at larger scales, where storing lots of raw time-series data and aggregating it over and over again becomes inefficient. The amount of value that PipelineDB adds is directly proportional to the amount of continuous aggregation that an analytics use case can benefit from. PipelineDB should be used for analytics use cases that only require summary data, like realtime reporting dashboards. PipelineDB is not a good fit for exploratory analytics on siloed datasets.
one_liner: Open-source time-series data analytics extension for PostgreSQL

launches.title: QuestDB - Data platform for mission-critical real-time workloads
launches.tagline: Where data cannot be lost and batch is too slow
launches.body:
### TL;DR

[QuestDB](https://questdb.com/) is the data platform for mission-critical workloads where data cannot be lost and batch processing is too slow. Banks, exchanges, energy companies and aerospace teams use it for real-time trading analytics, grid monitoring, fleet telemetry and mission operations. It handles millions of events a second and keeps years of history queryable.

In [QuestDB Enterprise](https://questdb.com/enterprise/), data tiers automatically to Parquet on object storage, replication and failover keep it available, and role-based access control governs who sees what. Run it in your own data centre, or in your own AWS or Azure account managed by our team (BYOC).

Try the [live demo](https://demo.questdb.io) with billions of rows.

### The Problem

Data that arrives fast and cannot be lost usually ends up spread across several systems. Teams run a message bus, a real-time store and a data lake for history, with glue code in between. Batch pipelines are too slow for decisions made while the market moves or the vehicle is in flight. Closed systems keep the data in formats and languages few people can use.

### How QuestDB solves it

One engine covers the whole path, from the live feed to the archive:

\- Capture: millions of events a second, with deduplication and out-of-order data handled on ingest.

\- Compute: materialized views, and live views in beta, compute on data as it lands.

\- Query: plain SQL with time-series joins (ASOF, WINDOW, HORIZON) across live data and history in one query. You or any of your agents can query it, through SQL or the QuestDB MCP server.

\- Retain: older data moves to Parquet on object storage automatically and stays queryable. Data also comes out fast in open formats: 500M rows into Apache Arrow in 2.3 seconds.

### Where it runs

\- Capital markets: market data and trades captured once, then pre-trade signals, TCA and markouts, intraday risk and surveillance on the full record.

\- Aerospace and robotics: telemetry from aircraft, rockets, satellites and robot fleets, monitored live and replayed in full.

\- Energy and infrastructure: readings from reactors, turbines and substations at full resolution, with anomalies flagged as they happen and years of history kept for regulators.

### Production deployments & Customers

7 of the largest 20 investment banks use QuestDB.

\- **Capital markets:** Ripple, OKX, Broadridge, Mizuho, Brevan Howard, Marex, Paxos, B3 (Brazil’s National Stock Exchange), SIX Group, Raymond James, HDFC Bank, One Trading, BTG Pactual, Laser Digital (Nomura), Selini Capital, Caladan, Danske Commodities, GTS Securities

\- **Aerospace:** Airbus, Firefly Aerospace, CesiumAstro, OpenC3, US Air Force

\- **Energy, industrial, Telco:** Bosch, Arbor Energy, Electio, Inductive Automation (Ignition's Core Historian runs on QuestDB), Airtel, NetApp, Weidmann, Copenhagen Atomics

See our [customers page](https://questdb.com/customers/) for more details.

launches.title: EdotEnv: Quant Neolab building towards RSI
launches.tagline: We turn markets into self-improving research environments for AI agents.
launches.body:
EdotEnv (YC S26) is a Quant Neolab building toward RSI. They turn markets into self-improving research environments for AI agents.

The path to RSI is a continuous loop: agents conduct experiments, learn from the results, and autonomously become better at conducting the next round of research. For that loop to continue, each round must present a harder problem than the last.

Markets create this dynamic naturally. Every discovered inefficiency attracts competition, and every successful strategy makes future opportunities harder to find. Markets therefore provide an advancing frontier for self-improving agents.

EdotEnv captures this process in multi-step environments where agents form hypotheses, design experiments, verify results and iterate. They use these environments to evaluate and post-train agents on increasingly difficult research tasks.

They work with frontier AI labs and academic groups building research harnesses, evaluation benchmarks, and post-training environments.

EdotEnv's team previously worked in quantitative research at G-Research, high frequency options trading at TransMarket Group, and LLM inference research at Etched.

If you're working on RSI, RL, post-training, or AI for research, reach out to them at [info@edotenv.com](mailto:info@edotenv.com).
